subject: Re: ClearPath Pay — inference budget priorities & batching options
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@clearpathpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: ClearPath Pay — inference budget priorities & batching options

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and clear next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call summary (high level):
- Primary pain: token spend volatility during peak authorization windows + customer-visible latency spikes when traffic bursts.
- Business goal: pilot to validate 30–40% unit-cost reduction and keep p95 latency under ~200ms for core 10–20 token prompts.
- Constraints: procurement is conservative — target pilot economics need to land at or below ~$25k/month to get approval for a 6–8 week technical trial.

Our proposed levers we discussed:
1) Batching: 4x–8x effective throughput uplift for similar latency envelope when aggregated at 50–100ms batching windows (saves ~20–30% on per-token GPU cost depending on model).
2) Prefix/KV caching: session-level prefix caching for authorizations and repeated user prompts — can cut API token generation by ~15–25% on typical flows.
3) Hybrid routing: route low-confidence/non-sensitive requests to a lower-cost model variant; keep high-confidence/PII-sensitive to private or dedicated pool.

Attachments: I attached a starter cost model (clearpath_cost_model_v1.xlsx) with the numbers we sketched on the call. Ben and I will follow up with a short SOW draft and a tighter ROI slide that maps to your average daily traffic.

Next steps (agreed):
- You: confirm procurement timeline and target approvers (procurement + CTO).
- Us: turn the workbook into a 1-page ROI and a 4-week pilot scope (Ben to prep SOW).
- Tentative pilot ask: sample traffic of ~250k tokens/day to start, ramp to 500k tokens/day over 4 weeks.

If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll aim to get the SOW & ROI back by Tues.

Thanks — Camila

Subject: Re: ClearPath Pay — inference budget priorities & batching options

Thanks Camila — good summary and appreciated. A couple clarifications from procurement/CTO side: 

1) Budget: procurement is asking us to target a pilot not to exceed $20k/month total operational spend. That’s the threshold for green-lighting a technical trial without a full capex commit. Can Redwood shape a pilot to meet that constraint?
2) SLA/latency: Mark (CTO) wants p95 below 200ms for the short prompts we discussed. If batching pushes us above that we’ll need a canary plan.
3) Stakeholders: I’m looping Mark (CTO) and procurement. Procurement would like any SOW to include an explicit exit clause if unit economics don’t meet the 30–40% reduction target.

Timeline: procurement committee meets July 29 — we need the SOW + an ROI slide by July 24 to get onto the agenda.

Also: security is a must; we’ll need SOC2 Type II evidence and a summary of data retention controls before procurement signs off. Happy to route that once you share links.

Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Product — ClearPath Pay
aisha.khan@clearpathpay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@clearpathpay.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearPath Pay — inference budget priorities & batching options

Hi Aisha — appreciate the clarity. A few targeted answers and a concrete pilot option that meets the constraints you called out.

Short answers:
- Yes — we can structure a limited pilot under $20k/mo if we scope traffic and use aggressive prefix caching + small-batch windows for latency-sensitive routes.
- p95 target of <200ms is achievable for the 10–20 token prompts if we reserve a small dedicated pool for latency-critical routes and use dynamic batching for non-latency-critical traffic.

Attached: SOW_Draft_v2.pdf and an updated cost tab in the drive (linked). Key assumptions used below — please flag if any are off: 
Assumptions (pilot baseline):
- Sample volume: 250k tokens/day initial (avg), 500k tokens/day peak after ramp.
- Baseline per-token infra cost (no batching, hosted model): $0.007/token.
- Batching + optimized kernels + 4-bit quantization reduces effective per-token infra cost to ~$0.0025/token for non-latency-critical calls.
- Prefix/KV cache reduces generated tokens by ~18% on your auth workflows (we measured similar patterns in other payments customers).

Simple ROI math (illustrative):
- Baseline monthly infra @ 500k tokens/day = 15M tokens/month * $0.007 = $105k/mo.
- With batching/quantization + caching (realistic pilot mix): effective tokens billed ~12.3M (after cache) and blended cost ~ $0.0029/token => ~$36k/mo.
- With additional routing to cheaper model for 25% low-risk traffic, blended cost approaches ~$28k/mo.

So — if we (a) commit to prefix caching and routing 25% of traffic to a lower-cost model and (b) reserve a small dedicated latency pool for the core flows, we can plausibly land near your $20k–$28k/mo range for a tightly scoped 4–6 week pilot. Exact numbers depend on traffic shape.

Pilot proposal (concrete):
Week 0: sign NDA & SOW, share sample logs (30k prompts) to validate cache hit rate.
Week 1–2: sandbox run (non-prod) to validate latency and cache behavior.
Week 3–4: live pilot with 10–20% traffic; scale to 50% if latency and unit-cost align.
Deliverables: 1-page ROI, weekly token burn dashboard, daily p95 latency report.

Questions we still need:
- Can you share a 7-day sample of typical prompt/response lengths (anonymized)? That drives batching benefit and cache hit-rate.
- Any specific regulatory constraints on routing to lower-cost variants?

We’ll turn this into a 1-page ROI and the SOW by Friday and add the SOC2/controls links.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — that aligns with what we discussed internally. A few commitments from our side: 

- We can provide an anonymized 7-day sample of prompts by Wed. That should let you finalize the ROI numbers quickly.
- Procurement confirms they’ll accept a timeboxed pilot with an exit clause; their preference is a not-to-exceed $20k/mo cap for the trial.
- Security: we’ll request SOC2 evidence and a short data-retention statement. Procurement will need the SOC2 link to attach to the SOW.

Mark (CTO) asked one operational ask: please include a canary policy that automatically routes fallback to a hosted (lower-cost) replica when dedicated pool latency > 250ms for more than 10 minutes. That ensures production safety and keeps UX intact.

If you can get an updated SOW + ROI in by Friday we’ll try to slot this for the July 29 procurement review.

Aisha
